title: Unauthorized access to the Q1 confidential draft

verdict.summary: david_m used sarah_j's account to grant himself access to the Q1 confidential draft, downloaded it once from his own workstation, and returned that night as her to take it a second time.
verdict.basis: Three of the six load-bearing claims are counting arguments over the full 180,800 lines rather than inference: one user/IP binding violation, one 400 and one 500, one call to /api/admin/role_update.

attacker.summary: Owns 10.0.8.45 across seven months of baseline. Denied the Q1 draft 80 times, then succeeded once.

victim.summary: Authorized reader of the asset with 1,528 ordinary successes. The only user in the file who ever appears on a second IP, and that IP is david_m's.

findings.claim: sarah_j's account was used from david_m's workstation.
findings.method: Nine of ten users appear on exactly one source IP across 180,800 lines. sarah_j is the only exception, and her second address is 10.0.8.45, which belongs to david_m. This is counting, not inference.

findings.claim: Ten login failures for sarah_j arrived from that workstation in two tight bursts, 23 hours apart.
findings.method: Exactly two clusters of four or more 401s inside ten minutes exist in the entire file, and both belong to sarah_j from 10.0.8.45. Her tightest gap between failures in the seven-month baseline is 809 seconds; inside these bursts it is 2.

findings.claim: david_m probed the forum endpoint three times before a payload was accepted.
findings.method: Status 500 and status 400 each occur exactly once in 180,800 lines, and both are his, 22 minutes apart. The third attempt returns 302, the ordinary redirect for a created post.

findings.claim: sarah_j's session performed a privileged role update one second after she opened post 1042.
findings.method: /api/admin/role_update appears once in the whole file. It is preceded at 11:07:56 by a view of forum post 1042 and followed at 11:07:59 by /assets/avatar_1042.png, a template that also appears exactly once. A one-second gap is machine latency, not a person navigating a console.

The logs record requests, never bodies or authorship. He created a post at 10:18:52 and read /intranet/forum/view/1042 three seconds later, and no other account touches object 1042 before sarah_j opens it. The object ID is never returned in a log field, so this is adjacency, not a recorded fact.

findings.claim: david_m downloaded the Q1 confidential draft once, after 80 denials, 19 minutes after the role update.
findings.method: 80 responses of 403 on that path to david_m across eight months, then exactly one 200, at 11:26:59 on 15 March. The two authorized readers hold 1,528 and 1,532 successes, which is what ordinary access looks like.

findings.claim: david_m was the grantee of that role update, added to the finance-confidential group.
findings.method: The log records sarah_j's account calling /api/admin/role_update but never records who was granted what. The seeded demonstration mailbox holds the automated notification that names him, sent one second later. Mailbox records corroborate a claim; headers are forgeable and we did not verify DKIM, so email alone never raises a finding above medium.

findings.claim: The account returned that night from the same workstation and took the file a second time.
findings.method: At 22:29:43 a login for sarah_j succeeds from 10.0.8.45 (the only success for her account from that host in the file), then dashboard, the zip, logout, inside four minutes.

findings.claim: The vector post was edited after the download, and a file he is authorized to read was fetched an hour later.
findings.method: POST /intranet/forum/edit/1042 at 11:48:01 and GET /finance/templates/expense.docx at 12:34:21. The edit is consistent with removing the payload and the second download with covering the first, but the logs carry neither body, so both readings remain open.

unknowns.text: How the login as sarah_j eventually succeeded. Ten failures, then a success from the same host, with no mechanism recorded anywhere in the log.
What post 1042 contained. The logs record requests, never bodies, so the payload is inferred only from its effect one second after the post was opened.
Whether david_m's group membership was revoked after the download. The file ends on 31 March with no further attempt on the asset, which is consistent with both revocation and simple caution.

dismissed.lead: Late-night access to the confidential draft
dismissed.why: Four of the five reads of that file outside 08:00-18:59 are benign: sarah_j at 07:00 in August, nicole_h at 21:17 in November and 19:00 in December, sarah_j at 00:19 on 6 March. Every one of them was an authorized reader on her own workstation. The hour of day does not separate the theft from ordinary work; the source IP does. The detector never reads hour-of-day.

dismissed.lead: Repeated denials as a signal on their own
dismissed.why: The file holds 5,324 responses of 403, spread from 506 to 545 per user across all ten accounts. Being refused a file here is ordinary permission friction, including michael_t refused this very asset from his own machine. What is not ordinary is the transition: 80 denials followed by exactly one success.

dismissed.lead: Failed logins as a signal on their own
dismissed.why: 899 login failures, 70 to 102 per account, near-uniform (including david_m failing his own login on the first day of the window). A wrong password is not evidence. Only two clusters of four or more failures inside ten minutes exist in the entire file, and both are sarah_j from a host she has never used.
